office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, including ferry funding, school funding, tax structure and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Four-term Democratic incumbent Dave Paul, chair of House Postsecondary Education & Workforce, faces Republican Tim Hazelo, a Navy veteran and contractor from Oak Harbor. They split on the income tax over $1 million, electric ferries and state spending.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative seeking a fifth term, a Skagit Valley College administrator who chairs the House Postsecondary Education & Workforce Committee.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 gas-tax package; voted against the 2025 services sales tax and B&O increases [S5][S7][S8][S9]
Says he is "fighting to fix our upside-down tax code" [S1]
Prioritizes funding three more electric ferries; voted for the 2025 clean fuel standard bill [S15][S11]
States he is pro-choice; voted for ESHB 1296 [S1][S6]

taxes.basis: Voted for the income tax over $1M and the gas-tax package and backs fixing the 'upside-down tax code', but voted against the 2025 services sales tax and B&O increases.

spending.basis: Voted for the 2025-27 operating budget; no stated spending philosophy beyond protecting college grant funding.

housing.basis: Voted for the 2025 rent-increase limits and names affordable housing a priority.

climate.basis: Voted for the 2025 clean fuel standard bill and prioritizes electric-ferry funding; endorsed by Sierra Club.

experience.basis: Seeking a fifth term, committee chair, with enacted bills; opponent has never held public office.

social.basis: Pamphlet states he is pro-choice; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no record on gender or sports policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which amended and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parents' rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Republican Navy veteran, contractor and truck driver from Oak Harbor and former Island County Republican chair, running against income taxes and electric ferries and for spending audits.
highlights: "No income taxes on Washington State residents!" [S3]
Calls for audits and transparency of every dollar spent [S3]
Opposes electric ferries as less dependable and costlier; favors diesel-electric boats [S6]
Would end cashless bail and cut housing regulations [S1]

taxes.basis: Platform opposes any income tax; Herald reports he opposes the millionaires' tax and any tax not approved by voters.

spending.basis: Calls for audits of every dollar, blames unsustainable spending for taxes, and questions social-program spending.

housing.basis: Would cut red tape and regulations he says drive up housing costs; no other housing proposals.

safety.basis: Would end cashless bail and 'catch and release'; no broader public-safety program.

climate.basis: Opposes the state's electric ferries in favor of diesel-electric on cost and reliability grounds.

experience.basis: No elected public office beyond precinct committee officer, challenging a four-term incumbent.
